data.raw_text:
🚨 ASIA TURNS BACK TO COAL AS LNG PRICES SPIKE AFTER IRAN CONFLICT.

Asian utilities are shifting from gas to coal as LNG prices jump after the US‑Israeli war on Iran disrupts shipments.

Spot LNG prices in Asia have doubled, with traffic through the Strait of Hormuz nearly halted and Qatar stopping exports.

Bangladesh is increasing coal power output and imports. Pakistan plans to rely more on domestic energy sources after recent solar additions helped stabilize supply.

The Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand are also boosting coal-fired generation to preserve limited LNG supplies. South Korea is lifting caps on coal output, and Japan’s JERA is keeping coal plants running at high rates.

Analysts expect high LNG prices and supply risks to continue, pushing more Asian countries toward coal despite long-term renewable goals.
